easy.def: A baby bear, lion or fox.
examples: The bear cub is cute.
A cub played in the grass.
The lion cub ran.

more.def: The young of some wild animals, such as bears, lions and foxes.
examples: The bear cub followed its mother through the woods.
A lion cub pounced on its sister's tail.
The fox cubs played outside the den.

easy.def: A small space or shelf for keeping your things.
examples: I put my coat in my cubby.
My cubby is by the door.
The cubby is small.

more.def: A small space or shelf where you keep your coat and things.
examples: I hung my backpack in my cubby.
Each child has a cubby with a name tag.
The cubbies are lined up along the wall.

easy.def: A solid shape with six square sides.
examples: A dice is a cube.
I stacked a cube.
The ice cube melted.

more.def: A solid shape with six equal square sides.
examples: A die is a cube.
I put an ice cube in my drink.
The box is shaped like a cube.

easy.def: A small space for one person to work.
examples: Dad works in a cubicle.
Her cubicle has a desk.
The cubicle is very small.

more.def: A small space in a large room that is separated by walls, where one person sits and works.
examples: My mom works at a desk in a small cubicle at the office.
Each worker had a cubicle with a computer and a chair.
The nurse stepped into the cubicle to check my ears.

easy.def: A bird that makes a sound like its name.
examples: A cuckoo sang in the tree.
The cuckoo clock chimed.
We heard a cuckoo.

more.def: A bird whose call sounds like its name, and which often lays its eggs in other birds' nests.
examples: We heard the call of a cuckoo in the woods.
A cuckoo lays an egg in another bird's nest and lets that bird raise the chick.
The little wooden cuckoo popped out of the clock on the hour.

easy.def: A long green vegetable that is crunchy.
examples: I ate a cucumber.
The cucumber is green.
Put cucumber in the salad.

more.def: A long vegetable with a dark green skin and a crisp, watery inside, often eaten in salads or made into pickles.
examples: We sliced a cucumber to put in the salad.
A cucumber is cool and crunchy and has lots of water inside.
Grandpa grew cucumbers and made pickles.

easy.def: To hold someone close in a warm, loving way.
examples: I cuddle my puppy.
She cuddled her doll.
We cuddled on the couch.

more.def: To hold or snuggle someone close for warmth or love.
examples: I cuddle my puppy every night.
She cuddled her doll and sang a lullaby.
We cuddled on the couch under a warm blanket.

easy.def: A warm hug.
examples: The baby wants a cuddle.
I gave her a cuddle.
A cuddle is nice.

more.def: A gentle, loving hug.
examples: The baby wants a cuddle from her mom.
I gave my little brother a cuddle after he fell.
A big cuddle can make you feel better.

easy.def: A signal to start.
examples: The actor waited for her cue.
The nod was my cue.
The music is the cue.

more.def: A signal for someone to begin doing something, such as speaking in a play.
examples: The actor waited for her cue to enter.
Her nod was my cue to start singing.
The bell was the cue for lunch.

easy.def: A long stick used in pool.
examples: He chalked the cue.
The cue is long.
He hit the ball with the cue.

more.def: A long, thin stick that is used to hit the ball in a game such as pool.
examples: He chalked the tip of the cue.
She aimed the cue at the ball.
The cue hung on the wall.

easy.def: The end of a sleeve.
examples: The cuff is wet.
My shirt has a button on the cuff.
I rolled up my cuff.

more.def: The band at the end of a sleeve or the folded edge at the bottom of a pant leg.
examples: I rolled up the cuffs of my sleeves.
The cuff on his shirt had a button.
Mud stuck to the cuffs of his pants.

easy.def: Having to do with cooking.
examples: She went to culinary school.
He has culinary skill.
The culinary class made soup.

more.def: Having to do with cooking or the kitchen.
examples: She studies at a culinary school to become a chef.
The chef showed off his culinary skills.
A culinary class taught us to bake bread.

easy.def: The one who did something wrong.
examples: The puppy was the culprit.
Who is the culprit?
We found the culprit.

more.def: The person or thing that is to blame for something wrong or a problem.
examples: The puppy was the culprit who had chewed the shoe.
We found the culprit: a loose wire was causing the problem.
The detective searched for the culprit.

easy.def: Having to do with the ways, art and customs of a group of people.
examples: We went to a cultural fair.
Food is part of our culture.
The cultural dance was fun.

more.def: Having to do with the ideas, art, music and customs of a group of people.
examples: We went to a cultural festival with food and dances from many countries.
The museum teaches about the cultural history of the region.
Food is an important cultural tradition in many families.

easy.def: The way of life of a group of people.
examples: Each culture has its own food.
We learned about another culture.
Music is part of culture.

more.def: The beliefs, customs, art and way of life shared by a group of people.
examples: Each culture has its own foods and holidays.
We read about the culture of ancient Egypt.
Art and music are part of every culture.

easy.def: Educated and knowing about arts.
examples: A cultured person likes art.
She is cultured.
The cultured man loved music.

more.def: Having good manners and a love of art, music and books.
examples: The cultured woman loved music and art.
He is a cultured person who reads many books.
The cultured hostess welcomed us.

easy.def: Clever, often in a sneaky way.
examples: The cunning fox tricked the crow.
She made a cunning plan.
The cunning cat caught the bird.

more.def: Clever at getting what you want, often by tricking others.
examples: The cunning fox tricked the crow into dropping the cheese.
She made a cunning plan to win the game.
The cunning cat waited quietly for the mouse.

easy.def: A small bowl with a handle for drinking.
examples: Drink from the cup.
I want a cup of milk.
The cup is full.

more.def: A small container with a handle that you drink from.
examples: She poured a cup of hot chocolate.
He drank a cup of milk with lunch.
The cup fell and broke.

easy.def: A way to measure food.
examples: Add one cup of flour.
Use two cups of water.
I need a cup of sugar.

more.def: A unit used in cooking to measure how much of something there is.
examples: The recipe calls for one cup of flour.
Add two cups of water to the pot.
Measure a cup of rice.

easy.def: A place with doors to keep dishes and food.
examples: The cups are in the cupboard.
Open the cupboard.
The cupboard is full.

more.def: A piece of furniture or a closed space with shelves and doors, where dishes, food or other things are kept.
examples: The plates are in the cupboard above the sink.
Mom keeps the cereal and crackers in the kitchen cupboard.
The old cupboard in the hall holds blankets and games.

easy.def: A small cake with icing on top.
examples: I ate a cupcake.
The cupcake has pink icing.
Mom baked cupcakes for my party.

more.def: A small cake baked in a paper cup, often with icing on top.
examples: Each cupcake had a sprinkle of colored sugar on top.
We baked a dozen cupcakes for the school bake sale.
She put a candle on her birthday cupcake and made a wish.

easy.def: The edge of the sidewalk next to the street.
examples: Stop at the curb.
He sat on the curb.
The car parked by the curb.

more.def: The raised edge of a sidewalk where it meets the street.
examples: Stop at the curb and look both ways before you cross.
The car parked next to the curb in front of our house.
We sat on the curb and ate ice cream.

easy.def: To hold back or control.
examples: I curb my temper.
We must curb our spending.
He curbed his appetite.

more.def: To hold something back or keep it under control.
examples: I tried to curb my laughing in class.
We must curb our spending until payday.
She curbed her temper and spoke calmly.

easy.def: Thick lumps that form in sour milk.
examples: Cheese is made of curds.
Curd is thick.
The curds were white.

more.def: The thick, soft part of milk that forms lumps when it turns sour and is used to make cheese.
examples: Cheese is made from curds.
The milk turned to curds and whey.
We ate cottage cheese, which is soft curds.

easy.def: Something that makes an illness go away.
examples: There is a cure.
The medicine is a cure.
Rest is a cure.

more.def: A treatment or remedy that makes a sickness go away for good.
examples: Doctors found a cure for the disease.
Rest is a cure for a cold.
Honey is a cure for a sore throat.

easy.def: To make a sick person well.
examples: The medicine cured him.
The doctor cures sick people.
The treatment cured her cough.

more.def: To make a sick person well again.
examples: The medicine cured his cough.
A good rest cured her headache.
The doctor cured the dog's infection.

easy.def: A time when you must be home.
examples: My curfew is at nine.
I got home before curfew.
Our curfew is when it gets dark.

more.def: A rule that says people must be home or off the streets by a set time.
examples: My older brother has a curfew of ten o'clock on weekends.
The town set a curfew so everyone would be home by dark.
Campers had a curfew, and lights went out at nine.

easy.def: Wanting to know or learn about things.
examples: The cat's curiosity got it into trouble.
Curiosity helped her learn.
Her curiosity grew.

more.def: A strong wish to learn or know about something.
examples: Curiosity led her to open the box.
The scientist's curiosity made her ask many questions.
The kitten's curiosity got it into trouble.

easy.def: Wanting to know more.
examples: The curious kitten looked in the box.
I am curious about what is in the bag.
The curious baby touches everything.

more.def: Eager to learn or find out about something.
examples: He was curious about how airplanes stay up in the sky.
Curious visitors gathered around the strange machine.
She was curious to know where the trail led.

easy.def: With wonder and interest.
examples: The cat looked curiously at the box.
He peeked curiously.
She asked curiously.

more.def: In a way that shows you want to know more.
examples: The squirrel peered curiously at the camera.
The children peeked curiously through the window.
She asked curiously about the old coin.

easy.def: A bit of hair that bends in a round shape.
examples: She has a curl on her head.
A curl fell over my eye.
He has red curls.

more.def: A small, round, bent shape, such as a lock of hair or a ribbon.
examples: A single golden curl hung down over her forehead.
A curl of smoke rose up from the campfire.
The baby had soft dark curls all over her head.

easy.def: To bend or twist into a round shape.
examples: The kitten curled up in my lap.
My hair curls when it is wet.
Leaves curl in the sun.

more.def: To twist into rings or round shapes, or to curve around something.
examples: The cat curled up on the sofa and fell asleep.
Heat made the edges of the paper curl.
The snake curled itself around a branch.

easy.def: A game played on ice with heavy stones.
examples: Curling is played on ice.
They play curling.
We watched curling.

more.def: A winter game in which players slide heavy stones across ice toward a target.
examples: Curling is played on ice with heavy stones.
Players sweep the ice in front of the stone in curling.
We watched curling on TV during the winter games.

easy.def: Having curls.
examples: She has curly hair.
The pig has a curly tail.
The ribbon is curly.

more.def: Full of small curves or curls.
examples: She has long, curly hair.
The pig's curly tail wagged.
The paper made curly shapes when I rolled it.

easy.def: The kind of money used in a country.
examples: Dollars are the currency here.
What currency do they use??
I changed my currency.

more.def: The type of money that is used in a country.
examples: The currency of the United States is the dollar.
I changed my money into the local currency when I arrived.
Each country has its own currency.

easy.def: Water or air that moves in one direction.
examples: The river has a strong current.
A current carried the boat away.
The ocean current is warm.

more.def: A steady flow of water, air or electricity in one direction.
examples: The strong current carried the leaf downstream.
Warm ocean currents flow past the island.
Electric current runs through the wire.

easy.def: Happening now.
examples: The current month is May.
His current job is baker.
Who is the current teacher?

more.def: Happening or being used at the present time.
examples: The current mayor has held the job for six years.
She told us about the current weather.
What is your current address?

easy.def: Right now.
examples: I am currently reading a book.
She is currently at school.
The store is currently closed.

more.def: At the present time.
examples: I am currently reading a book about space.
The store is currently closed for repairs.
He is currently in third grade.

easy.def: All the lessons taught in a school.
examples: Our school has a new curriculum.
Art is part of the curriculum.
The curriculum has math and reading.

more.def: The set of subjects and lessons that a school teaches.
examples: Music and art are part of our school curriculum.
The teachers planned a new science curriculum.
The curriculum for third grade includes fractions and geography.

easy.def: A spicy food made with sauce.
examples: We ate curry for dinner.
The curry is spicy.
Dad made chicken curry.

more.def: A dish from India and other places that is cooked with spices and a thick sauce, often served with rice.
examples: We had vegetable curry with rice for dinner.
The curry smelled of warm spices like cumin and turmeric.
She stirred the pot of curry slowly.

easy.def: A rude word, or a wish for bad luck.
examples: The witch put a curse on him.
It was a curse in the story.
The curse was broken.

more.def: A magic spell that brings bad luck, or a rude word said in anger.
examples: In the story, a witch put a curse on the castle.
The curse was broken at midnight.
The knight lifted the curse.

easy.def: To say rude words.
examples: Do not curse.
He cursed when he dropped it.
She never curses.

more.def: To use rude words, or to wish bad luck on someone.
examples: It is rude to curse in front of others.
He cursed when he stubbed his toe.
In the tale, the witch cursed the prince.

easy.def: A piece of cloth that hangs over a window.
examples: Close the curtain.
The curtain is blue.
The curtains are open.

more.def: A piece of cloth that hangs to cover a window or a stage.
examples: Close the curtains so the sun does not wake us.
The curtain rose and the play began.
The curtains in my room are blue.

easy.def: A polite bow where a girl bends her knees.
examples: She made a curtsy.
The curtsy was neat.
A curtsy is polite.

more.def: A polite bow in which a person bends the knees with one foot back.
examples: She made a curtsy to the queen in the play.
The girl gave a polite curtsy.
A curtsy is an old-fashioned greeting.

easy.def: To bend your knees as a bow.
examples: She will curtsy.
The girl curtsied.
He taught her to curtsy.

more.def: To bend the knees as a polite bow, with one foot behind.
examples: She curtsied to the queen in the play.
The girl curtsied after her dance.
The children curtsied and bowed to their guests.

easy.def: A bend that is not straight.
examples: The road has a curve.
A curve in the river.
The ball went in a curve.

more.def: A line or path that bends smoothly, not straight.
examples: The road has a sharp curve.
The river makes a big curve.
The ball flew in a curve.

easy.def: To bend smoothly.
examples: The road curves.
The path curved.
The river curves around the hill.

more.def: To follow a smooth bend, not a straight line.
examples: The road curves along the cliff.
The path curved around the lake.
The ball curved into the net.

easy.def: Bent in a smooth line, not straight.
examples: The road is curved.
A curved line.
The banana is curved.

more.def: Bent in a smooth line, like a bow or a circle.
examples: The curved road wound up the hill.
A banana has a curved shape.
He drew a curved line on the page.

easy.def: A soft pillow that you sit or lean on.
examples: I sit on a cushion.
The cushion is soft.
The cat sleeps on a cushion.

more.def: A soft bag or pad that you sit or lean on, or that protects something from hard bumps.
examples: I sat on a soft cushion on the floor.
The cat slept on the sofa cushion.
A thick cushion kept the vase from breaking.

easy.def: To soften a hit or fall.
examples: The pillow cushions my fall.
The snow cushioned the fall.
Grass cushions the fall.

more.def: To make something softer or easier to bear, such as a hit or a bump.
examples: The soft snow cushioned her fall.
The thick grass cushioned the landing.
A helmet cushions your head if you fall.

easy.def: Easy and comfortable.
examples: A cushy chair.
He has a cushy job.
The cushy bed is soft.

more.def: Easy and comfortable, with little work or trouble.
examples: He found a cushy spot on the couch.
She has a cushy job with little to do.
The cushy seats were soft.

easy.def: A soft, sweet food made from milk and eggs.
examples: I ate custard.
The custard is yellow.
We had custard for dessert.

more.def: A soft, sweet food made by cooking milk, eggs and sugar.
examples: We had warm custard for dessert.
Grandma made custard with vanilla.
The custard pie was smooth and creamy.

easy.def: A person who takes care of a building.
examples: The custodian cleaned the school.
A custodian fixed the door.
The custodian is kind.

more.def: A person whose job is to clean and take care of a building, such as a school.
examples: The custodian mopped the hallway after the rain.
A custodian unlocks the school each morning.
The custodian fixed the broken light in the gym.

easy.def: A usual way of doing something.
examples: It is a custom to shake hands.
That is a family custom.
The custom is old.

more.def: A way of doing something that people have done for a long time.
examples: It is a custom to give flowers on birthdays.
We have a family custom of walking on Sundays.
The custom began long ago.

easy.def: A person who buys things.
examples: The customer paid.
A customer came in.
The shop has many customers.

more.def: A person who buys goods or services from a shop or business.
examples: The customer paid for the loaf of bread.
A customer asked the clerk a question.
The bakery has many customers every morning.

easy.def: Made just the way you want.
examples: A customized shirt.
The customized cake.
A customized bike.

more.def: Made or changed to fit what a particular person wants.
examples: She wore a customized shirt with her name on it.
The customized cake was shaped like a dog.
He rode a customized bike with a bell.

easy.def: Special ways of doing things that a group follows.
examples: Every land has its own customs.
We learn about customs.
A custom of the holiday.

more.def: The traditional ways that a group of people do things.
examples: Every country has its own customs.
We learned about the customs of Japan.
Giving gifts is a custom on birthdays.

easy.def: The place where officials check bags at a border.
examples: We went through customs.
The customs officer looked at the bag.
The customs line was long.

more.def: The place at an airport or border where officials check what people bring into a country.
examples: We went through customs at the airport.
The customs officer checked our bags.
Officials at customs asked where we had traveled.

easy.def: To use something sharp to split or open.
examples: Cut the paper.
She cut the cake.
I cut the string.

more.def: To use a sharp tool to split, open, or take off a piece of something.
examples: Please cut the apple into four pieces.
He cut a long piece of string for the kite.
The barber cut my hair very short.

easy.def: A small hurt made by something sharp.
examples: I have a cut.
She has a cut on her hand.
A cut can sting.

more.def: An opening or injury made by something sharp.
examples: She had a small cut on her finger from the paper.
The nurse put a bandage on the cut.
He made a straight cut in the cloth.

easy.def: Sweet and fun to look at.
examples: The puppy is cute.
The kitten has cute ears.
Her hat is cute.

more.def: Pretty or sweet in a way that makes people smile.
examples: The kittens looked cute in their little hats.
What a cute baby!
She drew a cute cartoon of a smiling cloud.

easy.def: A person or pet who is very sweet and cute.
examples: The puppy is a cutie.
She called the baby a cutie.
What a cutie you are!

more.def: A person or animal that people think is especially cute or sweet.
examples: Grandma called the little baby a cutie and gave her a kiss.
The kitten was such a cutie that everyone wanted to hold it.
Look at that cutie asleep in her tiny blanket!

easy.def: A limit or a point where something stops.
examples: The cutoff is Friday.
The cutoff date is soon.
Sign up before the cutoff.

more.def: A limit or point at which something ends.
examples: The cutoff for sign-ups is Friday.
The cutoff date for the forms is noon.
A cutoff point is set for the test.

easy.def: A tool that cuts.
examples: The cutter cuts the cake.
A cookie cutter.
The cutter is sharp.

more.def: A tool or person that cuts things.
examples: I used a cookie cutter to make stars.
The paper cutter is sharp.
The wire cutter snipped the fence.
